chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever Allah accepts from him one prayer, He will not punish him, and whoever from whom He accepts a good deed, He will not punish him.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Allah accepting a single prayer or good deed?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a foundational principle in Shia theology that the acceptance (qabul) of a single prayer serves as a definitive guarantee against Hellfire. This narration underscores the concept of 'tawassul' through accepted deeds, suggesting that divine acceptance of one act of worship validates the sincerity of the believer, thereby securing their ultimate salvation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one from whom Allahazwj Accepts one Salāt, Heazwj would not Punish him, and the one from whom Heazwj Accepts a good deeds, Heazwj would not Punish him’’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
whoever 5 s one Salah (prayer) Allah accepts He does not punish him and whoever 5 s one good deed He accepts He does not punish him. 55
